correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts the mixed-side and one-side cases. For mixed sets, the domination step leaves at most two specifically indexed vertices and the \(n\ge3\) spare index supplies the first force. For a one-side set, after domination the exact number of unobserved neighbors of each opposite-side vertex is \(r\) or \(r-1\), where \(r\) is the number omitted from that side, so forcing succeeds exactly for \(r\le2\) (with the \(n=3\) singleton boundary checked separately). The resulting disjoint counting formula gives the stated polynomial. Exhaustive simulation for \(3\le n\le8\) matched the classification and every coefficient.

value.rationale: The all-set classification is a natural exact refinement of the minimum-focused crown problem and of the general power-domination-polynomial program. It determines every coefficient, the total number of feasible PMU placements, and the exact minimum-set multiplicity, while exposing the sharp structural distinction between mixed-side and one-side placements. This is an infinite-family structural theorem rather than a recomputation of one scalar parameter.
